clue.text: Best wishes for the goalie

parts.note: a parting wish for good health, read as advice to a goalkeeper to guard the net skilfully

explanation.surface: A fan sends a message of encouragement to the team's goalkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: The farewell phrase splits into a pun: a goalkeeper 'keeps' goal, so wishing one to keep well sounds like footballing advice.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a conventional sign-off expressing a wish for good health, i.e. best wishes.

clue.text: Spirited music?

parts.note: lively music on the surface, but 'spirited' hints at ghosts, so a tune that lingers in the mind like a spectre

explanation.surface: A short description of lively, energetic music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirited' means lively, but here it suggests ghosts: a refrain that haunts you is music possessed by spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunting tune is memorable and eerie, and a ghost haunts; the question mark flags this playful reading of spirited.

clue.text: Father of the Parisian, one from an Italian city

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
du is French for 'of the'
a means one, as in 'a dog'

explanation.surface: A French priest is said to come from a city in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' signals French: DU is French for 'of the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Padua is a university city in the Veneto region of northern Italy.

clue.text: Only a third of the footage, numerically speaking

definitions.text: Only a third of the footage, numerically speaking

parts.words: Only a third of the footage, numerically speaking
parts.note: a length measured in units each worth three feet gives a number one third the size of the same length counted in feet

explanation.surface: A film editor complains that only a third of the shot film survived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Footage' suggests film, but read it as a length counted in feet; the same length in three-foot units has a figure one third as large.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is a distance measured in yards, and a yard is three feet, so the number is a third of the footage.

clue.text: Most unfair

parts.note: unfair taken as the opposite of fair in its old sense of beautiful, so least attractive

explanation.surface: A protest that something is grossly unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfair' looks like unjust, but fair once meant beautiful, so the unfairest are the least good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the poetic sense means beautiful, so the most unfair are the least beautiful in appearance.

clue.text: Pull out of the old country

parts.note: ex- means former or old, as in ex-wife
a tract is an area of land or country

explanation.surface: Someone is withdrawing troops from a former nation.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something is to draw or pull it out, as a dentist removes a tooth.

clue.text: Room for games at home

parts.note: a sitting room in a house, the setting of the traditional indoor party games named after it

explanation.surface: A request for space in the house where the family can play games.
explanation.walkthrough: Charades and similar indoor pastimes are traditionally called 'parlour games', after the front sitting room where they were played.
explanation.definitionFit: A parlour is a sitting room in a private house, where indoor party games were traditionally played.

clue.text: Being sixteen puzzled engineers

indicators.note: puzzled means confused or muddled, so the letters of sixteen are jumbled

parts.note: CE stands for Civil Engineer(s)

explanation.surface: A sixteen-year-old is baffled by a group of engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puzzled' rearranges SIXTEEN into EXISTEN; CE is the abbreviation for civil engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being and existence are synonyms, both meaning the state of living or being real.

clue.text: Players' boss

parts.note: the person in charge of a group of musicians, not of sportsmen or actors

explanation.surface: A reference to whoever manages a sports team or theatre troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests sportsmen or actors; here they are musicians, and their boss heads the group.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who leads a group of musicians is in charge of those players.

clue.text: To plunder another subordinate scheme

indicators.note: another signals a different arrangement of the same letters of to plunder

explanation.surface: Criminals hatch a second, minor plan to rob somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' rearranges TO PLUNDER into another word with the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An underplot is a secondary plot in a play or novel, a subplot beneath the main story.

clue.text: Right continent backing last Soviet leader's wife

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the continent's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Asia is a continent

explanation.surface: A political commentator links a right-wing continent to a Soviet first lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ASIA into AISA after R.
explanation.definitionFit: Raisa Gorbachev was married to Mikhail Gorbachev, the final head of the Soviet Union.

clue.text: One or two items for consumption in the afternoon

definitions.text: One or two items for consumption in the afternoon

parts.words: One or two items for consumption in the afternoon
parts.note: a single bun, or read as two separate things: the drink and the sweet baked food served at an afternoon meal

explanation.surface: A description of some snacks eaten at an afternoon gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is one item, a bun, but split it and you get two items served at teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a sweet bun eaten at teatime; split, its halves name a drink and a baked treat.

clue.text: Spoon later found in the drink

indicators.note: found in tells us the word for later sits inside the word for the drink

parts.note: ale is a type of beer, a drink
post- means after or later, as in postwar

explanation.surface: A spoon is discovered afterwards at the bottom of a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: An apostle spoon is a traditional silver spoon with a figure of an apostle on the handle.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle spoon has a small saint's figure on its handle, so the word can stand for that kind of spoon.

clue.text: Pouch makes up most of the large bag

indicators.note: most of means the word is used without its final letter

parts.note: a sack is a large bag

explanation.surface: A pouch accounts for most of what goes in a big bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter K from SACK.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a sac is a bag-like cavity or pouch in an animal or plant.

clue.text: In the best position to make contact?

definitions.text: In the best position to make contact?

parts.words: In the best position to make contact?
parts.note: contact read as physical touching, so the one located closest to something

explanation.surface: Someone seems well placed to get in touch with a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make contact' suggests getting in touch; read literally, whoever is closest is best placed to touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the closest of all puts you in the best position to touch something, so the superlative of near fits.

clue.text: Great wolf twinkling in the evening sky

indicators.note: twinkling suggests flickering movement, so the letters of great wolf shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A star constellation shaped like a great wolf twinkles in the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twinkling' rearranges GREAT WOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: Afterglow is the light lingering in the western sky after sunset, seen at dusk.

clue.text: Girl from eastern America getting up

indicators.note: in a down entry getting up means the letters read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A girl from the east coast of the USA wakes and rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns EUS upwards, giving SUE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sue is a female first name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Aware of rocky peak first in Canadian city

indicators.note: first places the peak at the front of the word for aware of

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or peak, especially on Dartmoor
to be onto something is to be aware of it

explanation.surface: A climber reaches a rocky summit near a city in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'onto' a scheme is to have found it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada and capital of Ontario.

clue.text: Old student left a room in a harem

indicators.note: left means went away, so the student departs from the word old

parts.note: taken as written, the word old itself
L, for learner, is a crossword standard for student

explanation.surface: An elderly student walks out of a room in a harem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' is not O here: the word OLD is spelt out and 'student left' removes L, leaving OD, then add A.
explanation.definitionFit: An oda is a chamber in a Turkish harem; odalisque, a female slave there, comes from the same word.

clue.text: Chatter about toothed wheel

indicators.note: about can mean around or in disorder, so the letters of chatter are moved round

explanation.surface: Gossip concerning a gear wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CHATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a mechanism with a toothed wheel and a catch that allows turning in one direction only.

clue.text: No "ahs" with an extraordinary shout of praise

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters of no ahs and an are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exceptional cheer is so loud nobody says 'ah'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges NO AHS plus AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is an exclamation of adoration and praise to God.

clue.text: Main tug?

parts.note: main as the sea, and tug as a vessel that pulls others, not the principal pull

explanation.surface: A question about the chief pull or wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like chief, but poetically it means the open sea; a tug there is a vessel that hauls others.
explanation.definitionFit: A towboat is a tugboat, used to tow or push barges and ships at sea.

clue.text: Uncomplaining person in the ward

definitions.meaning: uncomplaining means tolerant and calm in the face of delay or trouble
someone receiving treatment in a hospital ward

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both enduring without fuss and someone under medical care in hospital.

clue.text: Head prevented inclusion of a small board

indicators.note: inclusion of means one word is enclosed in another, here the head taking in the word for prevented

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
let in its old sense means hindered or prevented, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Someone's head stopped a small board from being included.
explanation.walkthrough: LET meaning hinder survives in 'without let or hindrance' and the tennis call.
explanation.definitionFit: A palette is a thin board on which an artist mixes paints.

clue.text: No end of doctrine at the public debate

indicators.note: no end of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: teaching is a doctrine or body of belief

explanation.surface: A public discussion about a doctrine seems to go on endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' looks like 'plenty of', but it removes the last letter G from TEACHING.
explanation.definitionFit: A teach-in is an informal public debate or lecture session on a topical issue.

clue.text: Eggs mostly ground

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: the Oval is a London cricket ground

explanation.surface: Eggs that have mostly been crushed into powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like crushed, but it is a sports ground: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground. 'mostly' drops its last letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the plural of ovum, a female reproductive cell or egg.

clue.text: Said number was somehow anticipated

indicators.note: said means spoken out, so the number is heard as a word sounding the same

parts.note: four is a number

indicators.note: somehow suggests in some unknown way, so the letters of was are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone claims a figure was predicted in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' turns FOUR into its sound-alike FORE; 'somehow' rearranges WAS into SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to anticipate, predicting something before it happens.

clue.text: Unauthorised divulgation from a drip?

definitions.meaning: a secret disclosed to the press without permission
the liquid escaping from a dripping tap or pipe

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both secret information escaping to outsiders and fluid escaping through a hole.

clue.text: Check into gold, said Parisian concluded

indicators.note: concluded says the French word comes at the end, finishing off the answer

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
dit is French for 'said'

explanation.surface: A French speaker announces that an investigation into gold is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' signals French: DIT means 'said'.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection of accounts, a check on their accuracy.

clue.text: Some are falling over exhausted

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters are taken from within the word falling

explanation.surface: Some things are toppling over through tiredness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes letters from inside fALLINg.
explanation.definitionFit: All-in is informal British for completely tired out.

clue.text: Had to care about the figures

indicators.note: about can mean in disorder, so the letters of had to care are mixed around

explanation.surface: Someone needed to worry about the numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figures' looks like numbers, but here it means solid shapes. 'about' rearranges HAD TO CARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Octahedra are solid shapes with eight faces, so they are geometric figures.

clue.text: Modern actors left with energy and joined the football team

parts.note: new means modern
the cast is the set of actors in a production
E is the symbol for energy in physics
united means joined together

explanation.surface: Fresh actors and a lively energy combined to form a football side.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWCASTLE UNITED is an English Premier League football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle United is a professional club playing soccer in north-east England.
